column2: BPO – What’s the Food Inside By: Junemard Quiban
column3:
Ever wondered how nocturnal people spend their lunch in the city? Quite a question for someone living in Davao, where night life is far different than that of New York. But how do these guys spend lunchtime in the dead of the night? Are the choices of food more than enough? Is it healthy? Is it scrumptious?

We were inside Alorica, the first call center sited in Matina IT Park, beside S&R. They have at least 6 concessionaires on the 2nd level of the building. After checking on it, I could say you should be able to figure out what you’ll eat and be satisfied about it.

These concessionaires try as much as they can to be unlike the rest of the gang.

First off – Green Leaf: they sell vegan dishes – salads with thousand island dips and Peta cheese. Even clubhouse sandwiches with lemon and cucumber juices to make your meal satisfying. Not pure vegan actually, included in their menu is chicken, pork or tuna garnish. Foods which will satisfy those vegetarian call center agents.

 

Next to it are DESSERTS! Who doesn’t love desserts? Cakes, puddings, brownies and more sweets! Aside from that, they even sell rice broth (arroz caldo) and noodle soup (batchoy) if you just had enough of having too many sweets.

Heavy meals are also served. Two of these concessionaires are selling viands with rice at a reasonable price. By reasonable we’re talking in a range of 35-50 PhP. You can choose from fried to soup viands. To name a few we have the famous adobo, sinigang, kilawin, caldereta, menudo, chicken curry and many more. If you think you’re overkilled with meat, veggies are there to save you! Pinakbet, chop suey, eggplant salad, even seaweeds like guso and lato. You can even choose every day to be fried day! Fried fish, pork or chicken! Barbecues don’t get left behind as well. Maybe chicken or pork, which sometimes would let you end up thinking over 80% of the population are strictly carnivorous… (Is it really?)

The rest of the two are mini stalls, selling steamed corncobs with butter, siomai, fried noodles and the like. All of these sellers also sell pica picas, junk food, bite sized chocolates, candies and many more! Of course, the all-time instant coffee is everywhere!  And you can just ask for a mug if you don’t have a tumbler with you.

You will be thinking these will be enough. Though I also need to give you a heads up, it’s not so much like a feeding frenzy during weekends. These sellers, well most of them, are closed on weekends. Since there’s a few headcount of call center employees during Saturdays and Sundays, they also make sure the food prepared don’t go over the expected head count.

Overall, it’s a festive day almost every day inside a call center pantry. At around 2 to 3 in the morning, where most of the agents are on lunch, it’s a crazy, fun and chatty meal time! One may not find it enough, especially when these are what you see 5 times a week for a few years, but going out may not be the best idea when only 24-hour fast foods are left open. So if you just think it’s just skimpy all over, then might as well bring your own food. ☺

column2: Davao Street food Madness! By Roland Matthew Acosta
column3:
Davao City is known for tons of things, But when it comes to its appetizing selection of streetfoods it will capture any  person’s heart. whether youre looking for a light snack or looking for a tummy-full. You dont need to go anywhere else but Davao City’s streets.

If you’re craving for sweets, there’s bannana cue, turon and kamote cue. Banana-cue is the banana version of this favorite Davao street food that is just as popular, while turon is also made banana cut lengthwise for faster cooking, wrapped in lumpia wrapper and deep fried. and kamote-cue is sweet potato sliced into chunks, coated with caramel syrup, fried and skewered with bamboo sticks.

Another type of Davao streetfood are Kwek-Kwek and fishballs. Kwek-kwek is a tempura-like Filipino street food made by deep-frying orange batter covered hard-boiled eggs which mny davaoenos love to eat. and fishball is another street food favorite among those who want a tasty snack. Fishballs are fried, skewered with bamboo sticks and dipped into a sweet, sweet and sour or spicy sauce which is loved by students and children.

If you really are looking for a hunger quenching foodtrip then here’s the streetfoods just for you! The Isaw or Chicken intestines are a really huge hit among the locals.it can be fried or barbecued, dipped in the same vinegar-based sauce  and eaten as a mid-afternoon snack or as a hunger satisfying dinner.

Davao streetfood is not only mouthwatering but also cheap and budget friendly, with only 50 pesos for a meal. it really is satisfying, its like the food costs almost like a giveaway. whether youre looking for a light snack or to have a hungry heavy foodtrip.

column2: Battleground: Dining and Gaming Cafe by Lara Advincula
column3:
Are you a gamer who also loves to eat? Already had enough only eating junk foods and drinking soft-drinks while playing ? Are you craving for more ? Well, good news for all gamer, like me, who are currently living here in Davao City. There’s a newly opened cafe located at Acacia St. Juna Subdivision, Matina Davao City(near Ateneo Junior High School) called Battleground. It’s the first gaming and dining place here in Davao City. Here you can satisfy your cravings while playing your favorite online game at the same time.

Looking from the outside you can tell that the exterior design is giving a more masculine vibe because of black and blue colors that they used. The interior design is also well-arranged considering the fact that it’s a gaming and dining cafe at the same time. Once you get inside you can also see some wallpapers consisting of different game and cartoon characters. And because it’s designed as a gaming cafe, they currently has 10 gaming PCs inside with a rate of P20/hr, P50/3hrs, and P100/6hrs. They will also give you a card in case you can’t consume all your time, so that you can still make use of it when you decide to come back. So, I assure you guys, that you will definitely enjoy playing at Battleground.

So, let’s take a good look at their restaurant now, shall we?

Battleground offers plenty of choices for you to eat. Even though their cafe is designed for gamer, you can also eat there together with your family and friends. They serve dishes like breakfast meals, burgers, fries and pasta. And of course it cannot be completed if there’s no desserts, right? Their restaurant also has a unique way on presenting their menu. They uses different game terms such as single or team, upgrades, level ups, and combos instead of using common terms. Let’s take a look at their menu:

Now here are some of the must-try foods at Battleground:

Chicken Wings (P90 single, P175 team) – At first bite, you can already taste the perfect blend of sweetness and spiciness of it. It’s a very addictive dish at a reasonable price. You may choose to add P20 for rice and dips,and etc.

Pizza Baguette (P210 single, P400 team) – A french bread cut in half with pizza toppings cooked on top. It’s not pricey because the taste is so delicious, it’s really worth the price.

Overall, Battleground is a great place to hang out and play for gamer, but it can also be a good place for family gatherings. They can serve foods for a whole family and barkadas. Battleground is a place for everybody who wants to have fun and enjoy.

column2: Home Cooked: Corn Shrimp with Veggies Soup by Joel Parojinog Jr.
column3:
This was  made by my mother. She’s not a professional chef but I can really tell she has the skills. She really made food better than the usual taste of it. She usually does some experiments in making the food more special. And this corn shrimp with veggies soup is one of the product of her own experiments.

Ingredients:

Shrimps
Corn/s
Sponge Gourd (Patola) leaves
Corchorus (Saloyot) leaves
Tomato
Chopped Green Onions
Ginger
Salt
Brown Sugar

Procedures:

To start, prepare the following ingredients listed above. The amount of ingredient needed for this recipe always depend on how much are you going to make. The first thing you need to do is to extract the natural water of the shrimps. After extracting, you may proceed on frying the shrimp but before you fry, don’t forget to put a small amount of oil on the frying pan. After heating the pan, put the shrimp on it. After putting it, stir the shrimp to avoid shrimp from sticking on the frying pan. Continue until it become a bit crispy, just a bit.
Then, for the soup, you need to boil a water (the amount depends on you). If the water already boiling, put first the corn then the rest of the ingredient including the shrimp but put the leafy veggies last. Stir the soup gently to mix well the ingredients but not for too long.
After a few minutes, you may now prepare it on the table and have a taste 😉.
